message:
fix(update): the update lock was a constant, so every test contended with the installed product

The assembly hardcoded Global\GNLinkUpdate. Every test that drove it took
the same machine-wide mutex the installed product uses -- and one run here
failed with "another update or installer holds the lock", which is that
collision happening. The other direction is worse: a test holding it would
keep a real update from starting on somebody's machine.

It is a dependency now, required by validate(), and production supplies
the machine-wide name while the suites supply session-scoped ones of their
own. The assembly test asserts that production still supplies the real
name, because turning a constant into a seam is exactly how a production
value quietly becomes something else.

Also, replacing the fixture with one that exits broke a control that
needed a process which does not. It asserted that deleting a running image
fails, and with the new fixture the image was usually no longer running by
the time the delete was attempted -- so it passed on timing. That control
now starts a copy of the command interpreter, directly, and stops it
through the handle it was given.

And when a shell-routed launch does not record itself, the note now says
which scenario fired it. "A launch never landed" with nothing to tie it to
is a note nobody can act on, and the directory it keeps alive gets charged
to the whole run instead of the case that caused it.
